claims.proposition_evaluated: At its meeting of 2026-08-26, the Infrastructure Committee (not City Council) carried a motion reducing the maximum time each approved public speaker could speak from the 5 minutes in section 38(1) of Bylaw 18155 (consolidated 2025-10-29) to a maximum of 3 minutes for that meeting, and the committee's list of approved speakers on item 7.6 (IS03688, Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration Program Update) held between 60 and 80 entries (primary count N, primary band).
claims.interpretation_notes: Read as the brief normalizes it. Every element of the Supported condition holds. (1) Standing limit: s.38(1) of Bylaw 18155: 'Each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of 5 minutes.' The last amendment noted under s.38 is S.15, Bylaw 20226, July 4, 2022. (2) The cut: under item 1.4, a motion moved by M. Janz says the committee will 'adjust the rules on time limits as set out in section 38 of Bylaw 18155' for the 2026-08-26 meeting so that 'each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of three minutes'. It carried 6 to 0. (3) Coverage: the motion's words reach 'each approved speaker' at the meeting. It is not limited to item 7.6 or to any class of speaker. (4) Primary count N = 64 (panels 15+15+15+15+4), inside 60-80. ALTERNATIVES (my calculations from the carried minutes, counting entries): (a) Alternative band 50-90 with N=64: Supported, so the row is unchanged. (b) N-all = 79, made up of item 7.1: 5; item 7.3: 1; item 7.4: 8 in the 2.3 motion plus 1 in the additional-speaker motion (4 to 0) = 9; item 7.6: 64. 79 is inside 60-80 and inside 50-90, so Supported under both, though 79 is one entry below the primary band's upper edge. A person approved on two items would appear twice in N-all, and the carried text cannot show whether anyone did. (c) N-spoke = 52 (presentation panels 16+16+18+2). That is outside the primary band 60-80, giving Partially supported (the count fails the magnitude rule while the 5-to-3 cut for every approved speaker holds). It is inside the alternative band 50-90, giving Supported. So the finding is DEFINITION-SENSITIVE: under N-spoke with the primary band the row changes from Supported to Partially supported. The story should say so beside the verdict. QUALIFICATIONS. Q1: The motion sits under item 1.4 (Adoption of Agenda), moved by M. Janz, and names section 38 of Bylaw 18155. Limits set: 3 minutes per approved speaker; for each member of Council, 3 minutes to ask questions and 3 minutes to speak to or close debate on a motion (standing limits 5 minutes each under s.38(5) and s.38(6)). In favour (6): E. Rutherford, A. Salvador, R. Clarke, M. Janz, A. Knack, A. Paquette. Opposed: none recorded. Carried 6 to 0. The motion does not cite s.4 or use the words 'special resolution'. Special resolution (s.2(2)(m)) needs at least two-thirds of all members of the Standing Committee. The minutes' header lists six members present, and roll call notes Mayor Knack is a member under s.15(3) of Bylaw 18156. My calculation: 2/3 x 6 = 4, and 6 in favour >= 4, so the requirement was met on the minutes' record. A larger membership of up to 9 would still be met. Q2: It applies to every approved speaker at the meeting, across all four items, not only item 7.6. Q3: In the minutes' order the motion is the third motion under item 1.4. It comes after the agenda-adoption and Orders of the Day motions, before the item 2.3 Requests to Speak motion, and before item 7.6. Item 2.4 made item 7.6 the first item of business, so the motion also comes before the first public speaker on 7.6. Q4: Item 2.3 for item 7.6 has 5 panels: P1 15 entries (2 with an organization: Edmonton Bike Coalition, YEG Bike Coalition); P2 15 (8: Bike Bus Alberta, Holyrood Voice, Holyrood Community 79 St Action Group, YEG Bike Coalition, Paths for People, Ward Métis Bikes x3); P3 15 (3: Let's Bike There YEG, Bike Edmonton, YEG Bike Coalition); P4 15 (2: Paths for People, YEG Bike Coalition); P5 4 (0). N = 64, of which 15 entries carry an organization. By organization: YEG Bike Coalition 4, Ward Métis Bikes 3, Paths for People 2, and one each for Edmonton Bike Coalition, Bike Bus Alberta, Holyrood Voice, Holyrood Community 79 St Action Group, Let's Bike There YEG and Bike Edmonton. No further additional-speaker motion for 7.6 appears in the carried items. Q5: N-all by item: 7.1 = 5 (5 with organizations: Edmonton Construction Association x3, Big Lake Community League, PCL Construction Management Inc.); 7.3 = 1 (Alberta Avenue Business Association); 7.4 = 9 (8 + 1 additional; 6 with organizations: Alberta Ecotrust Foundation x2, Solar Alberta x2, Big Lake Community League, BILD Edmonton Metro); 7.6 = 64. Total 79. Q6: Presentations under 7.6, in 4 panels: P1 16 entries (5 with organizations: YEG Bike Coalition x2, Holyrood Voice, Holyrood Community 79 St Action Group, Paths for People); P2 16 (6: Bike Bus Alberta, Ward Métis Bikes x2, Let's Bike There YEG, Bike Edmonton, Paths for People); P3 18 (1: YEG Bike Coalition); P4 2 (0). N-spoke = 52, of which 12 entries carry an organization. Presentation panels are numbered and composed differently from the Requests to Speak panels. N = 64 and N-spoke = 52 are reported side by side; no difference is computed. Q7: The carried items record no speaker given more or less than the limit and no motion extending any speaker's time. 5 public-speaker attachments are listed under item 7.6 (attachment entries 11-15, labelled Panel 3, 2, 1, 4, 3; titles not reproduced). Q8: No City record stating a reason for the motion was identified (search described in limitations). Q9: No earlier meeting since 2025-10-29 adjusting s.38 was identified, but my search was not systematic (see limitations).

limitations: My own fetch of the post-meeting minutes URL returned HTTP 403, and of the bylaw PDF HTTP 502, on 2026-10-02. All counts and quotations come from the carried copies (YF-EV-0209 minutes, YF-EV-0210 agenda, YF-EV-0251 bylaw), which every reviewer received. Agreement on their content is not independent retrieval. Minutes date of record: the carried copy, read 2026-10-02.
The carried minutes contain no later correction to items 1.4, 2.3 or 7.6, and do not show whether the minutes have since been approved at a later meeting. I could not check the live page.
Formatting in the carried text: the first entry under each item or panel is prefixed '- - '. I took this as a list-nesting artefact and counted it as one entry.

Presentation Panel 4 under item 7.6 lists only 2 entries, then goes straight to the A. Salvador motion. I cannot tell from the carried text whether that panel is complete or the carried rendering is truncated. If truncated, N-spoke would be higher than 52.

Names are withheld, so entries cannot be matched across lists. N-spoke may include people who registered after the 2.3 motion (the agenda notes the public 'can request to speak up until your item has been dealt with'), and N-all may count one person twice.

Under s.3(c) of Bylaw 18155, the establishing bylaw for a Standing Committee (Council Committees Bylaw 18156) prevails where it conflicts. My fetch of C18156.pdf returned 502, so I could not confirm it sets no different speaker limit. The motion itself treats s.38 as the applicable rule.

Amendments after 2025-10-29: a consolidation cannot list amendments made after its own date. Web searches found none to s.38 in force on 2026-08-26. A search summary mentioned a Bylaw 21631 ('Council and Committee Meeting Agendas') on the 2026-09-08 Council agenda. I did not read it, and it postdates the as-of date in any case.

Q8 (reason for the motion): none identified. Searched the carried minutes and agenda items, the Taproot Edmonton agenda preview of 2026-08-24, the CBC/Yahoo report of 2026-08-26 (the CBC original returned 403), and web searches for the motion's wording, as of 2026-10-02. The 22 uncarried items of the minutes were not seen.

Q9 (earlier adjustments to s.38 since 2025-10-29): none identified. This absence is weak. The eScribe portal returned 403, so I could not page through minutes, and a web search for the motion's exact wording returned no City record.

The holder wrote '70 is in the current cue' in present tense, in the days after the meeting, without naming a meeting. It could conceivably refer to a later meeting's speaker list. The brief fixes the 2026-08-26 meeting, and the count of 64 fits that reading.
One web search returned links to pull requests in this project's own repository about earlier runs. I did not open them or use them, so this review stays blind.
The CBC article's photo credit names a person. That was not copied beyond this note, and no member of the public is named here.

calculations_needed: N (item 7.6, 2.3 motion) = 15 + 15 + 15 + 15 + 4 = 64 entries, of which 2 + 8 + 3 + 2 + 0 = 15 carry an organization (reviewer's count).
N-all = 5 (7.1) + 1 (7.3) + 9 (7.4: 8 + 1 additional) + 64 (7.6) = 79 entries (reviewer's count). It may double-count a person approved on two items.
N-spoke (item 7.6 presentations) = 16 + 16 + 18 + 2 = 52 entries, of which 5 + 6 + 1 + 0 = 12 carry an organization (reviewer's count).
Bands: N=64 is inside 60-80 and 50-90. N-all=79 is inside 60-80 and 50-90. N-spoke=52 is outside 60-80 and inside 50-90.
Special resolution: 2/3 x 6 members = 4. The vote was 6 in favour, which meets it (reviewer's calculation, using the minutes' attendance of six members).
what_would_change_my_verdict: A correction to the published minutes changing the item 1.4 motion's limit, coverage or result, or the item 2.3 list for 7.6 so that N falls outside 60-80.
An amendment to s.38, or a conflicting provision in Bylaw 18156, in force on 2026-08-26 that set a standing limit other than 5 minutes. That would make the verdict Partially supported.
Adopting N-spoke as the measure of the queue. Under the primary band that would make the row Partially supported.
claims.suggested_one_line: Yes. For the Aug. 26 meeting, the Infrastructure Committee voted 6–0 to cut each speaker from the bylaw's five minutes to three, and 64 people were approved to speak on the bike-lane item.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Supported. The Council Procedures Bylaw gives each approved speaker five minutes. At the start of its 2026-08-26 meeting, the Infrastructure Committee (not full Council) voted 6–0 on a motion by Coun. M. Janz to cut that to three minutes for every speaker at the meeting. The same motion cut councillors' question and debate time to three minutes. The committee's list had 64 entries approved to speak on the bike-lane item, within 'about seventy'. 79 were approved across all four items, and 52 are recorded as having presented on the bike-lane item. If you count only the people who presented, 52 falls short of the 60–80 range, so the count part depends on the definition used. The minutes give no reason for the cut. They do not show whether speakers were for or against the lanes, whether they were complainants, whether three minutes was enough, or whether anyone's concerns were ignored.
suggested_tldr: The bylaw's standing limit is 5 minutes per speaker (s.38(1), Bylaw 18155).
The Infrastructure Committee voted 6–0 under item 1.4 to set 3 minutes per approved speaker for the 2026-08-26 meeting.
64 entries were approved to speak on the bike-lane item (79 across the meeting); 52 are recorded as presenting.
If the queue means people who actually presented (52), the count falls outside the 60–80 range.
The minutes record no reason for the cut and no speaker's position.
